summary.text: Meta Platforms (formerly Facebook, Inc.) owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp. Founder Mark Zuckerberg controls a majority of shareholder voting power through high-vote Class B stock. In 2019 the FTC imposed a $5 billion penalty on Facebook over privacy violations. In December 2020 the FTC and a coalition of 48 state and territorial attorneys general filed separate antitrust suits over its acquisitions of Instagram and WhatsApp. In November 2025 a federal judge ruled that the FTC had not shown Meta currently holds monopoly power; the FTC has appealed.

facts.claim: On December 9, 2020, the FTC sued Facebook, alleging it illegally maintained a monopoly in personal social networking, partly by acquiring Instagram (2012) and WhatsApp (2014). That same day a bipartisan coalition of 48 attorneys general, led by New York, filed a separate antitrust suit. In November 2025, Judge James Boasberg ruled that the FTC had not shown Meta currently holds monopoly power.

facts.claim: Each share of Meta's Class B common stock carries ten votes and each Class A share carries one. Meta's 10-K describes founder Mark Zuckerberg as controlling a majority of the voting power of its outstanding capital stock.

connections.claim: Peter Thiel made Facebook's first outside investment, putting in $500,000 in 2004 at a $5 million valuation. He served on its board from April 2005 until Meta's 2022 annual meeting.

connections.claim: Reid Hoffman invested in Facebook's first outside funding round in 2004. TechCrunch reported his stake as $37,500 at a $5 million valuation. Hoffman has said he declined to lead the round because of his other social-networking roles and suggested that Peter Thiel lead it instead.
